title: What is the cloud?
examples: If I save a photo to the cloud, is it really on the internet?
Are data centres in every city, or only in big places?
What is the difference between just storing data and running an app in the cloud?

explain.say: The cloud is not really a physical cloud in the sky.

items: It is a way to use computers over the internet.
It lets you access files from anywhere.
It uses someone else's powerful computers.

explain.say: These services run inside huge buildings called data centres.
Data centres contain many powerful computers called servers.
This means you are using other people's computers for your tasks.
When you use online video calling, you are using the cloud.
A common mistake is thinking the cloud means no physical location.

faq.q: Where exactly is the cloud located?
faq.a: The cloud is not in the sky; it is located in large buildings called data centres. These centres house thousands of powerful physical computers.
asks: Is the cloud somewhere in the air?
Do I need to visit the cloud to use it?

faq.q: What is the difference between storing data and running software in the cloud?
faq.a: Storing is like renting a digital filing cabinet for your files. Running software means the actual program is active on the remote computers for you to use.
asks: Is storage and computing the same thing?
If I run a program, is it just using my phone's power?

faq.q: Are data centres in every country?
faq.a: Major cloud providers have data centres in many countries, but they are built in large, secure, and well-connected locations.
asks: Do all countries have cloud servers?
Why are some places better for data centres?

faq.q: Do I need to be connected to the internet to use the cloud?
faq.a: Yes, you must have an active internet connection to send requests to and receive data from the remote servers in the cloud.
asks: Can I use the cloud offline?
What happens if my internet goes down?

faq.q: Are cloud services always safe from hacking?
faq.a: Data centres have very high levels of physical and digital security, but users must still use strong passwords and keep their own data secure.
asks: Who keeps the cloud data safe?

facts: Data centres are large, specialized buildings designed to house and operate computing equipment.
Cloud computing allows users to access computing resources, like storage and software, over the internet.
Servers are the physical machines within a data centre that process data and run applications.
The internet acts as the connection pathway between your device and the remote data centres.

quiz.say: When you use a service like Gmail, where is your email actually stored and processed?
quiz.why: Gmail uses remote servers in a data centre to store and manage your emails for you.

wrong.0: Routers only direct the connection; they do not have enough space for all your emails.
wrong.1: The internet is the pathway, not the storage location for the actual data.
wrong.3: This is wrong because if you lose your phone, the emails would be lost too.

quiz.say: If a company runs its website using cloud services, what physical location is doing the heavy lifting?
quiz.why: Websites need powerful, constant electricity and cooling, which only data centres can provide reliably.

wrong.0: The exchange point only connects networks; it does not run the actual website software.
wrong.2: Offices are for people; data centres are for machines that run 24/7.
wrong.3: A personal computer is too small and lacks the necessary backup power.

quiz.say: What is the most accurate description of 'the cloud' in technology?

options.show: A network of remote computing services
options.say: A network of remote computing services

options.show: A magical place with no wires
options.say: A magical place with no wires

quiz.why: This definition covers both the physical location (data centres) and the concept (remote service).

wrong.1: This is too imaginative; cloud computing relies entirely on physical wires and electricity.
wrong.2: This only covers storage; it ignores the ability to run complex programs remotely.
wrong.3: The internet is the medium, but the cloud is the specific service being delivered over that medium.
